newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada mutual fund sales hit C$9.7 bln in June.
newsitem.headline: Canada mutual fund sales hit C$9.7 bln in June.

text.p: The Investment Funds Institute of Canada said on Tuesday that gross sales for all funds totaled C$9.7 billion in June.
It said the total number of assets managed by members of the mutual fund industry in Canada rose to C$258.6 billion for a total of 28.8 million accounts.

"The mutual fund industry has experienced incredible sustained growth over the last six months," said Tom Hockin, president and chief executive of the Investment Funds Institute of Canada (IFIC). "The continued growth of the industry indicates that investors are taking a longer view in investing while maintaining a strategy of dividing savings among various asset classes."

Investors Group topped IFIC's list of the 73 mutual funds in Canada with C$29.4 billion of assets under administration, closely followed by Trimark Investment Management Inc with C$25.9 billion and Royal Mutual Funds Inc with C$22.6 billion.

IFIC said the highest amount of assets were concentrated in Canadian equity funds, which have grown to C$76.1 billion by the end of the second quarter in 1997 from C$45.9 billion in 1996. Foreign equity investments rose to C$55.3 billion in 1997 from C$39.1 billion, while balanced funds rose to C$38.1 billion from C$23.7 billion and U.S. equity funds rose to C$10.5 billion from C$6.5 billion.

Canadian brokers and dealers dominated the industry with 46.4 percent of the mutual fund pie in Canada, followed closely by the major banks with a 25.5 percent slice and mutual fund agencies had 11.1 percent. The other 17 percent was made up from trust companies, direct sales to the public, unions, life insurance companies and credit unions.
